body:
Evaluate and add fleet orchestration on top of the ADLC so parallel development is a first-class, executable capability — not just doctrine. Today the lifecycle runs linearly (one ticket per interactive session) even though the doctrine and data model already contemplate parallelism: ADLC.md describes P4 as "parallel worktrees, single writer per partition", merge-forecast certifies fan-out width from the ticket DAG, and @adlc/core already ships topoSort/computeFloat/scopesOverlap over .adlc/tickets.json edges. What is missing is the orchestrator that dispatches ready tickets to headless workers and walks them through the gates.

=== REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION (read first, generalize — do not fork) ===
A working, agy-specific fleet orchestrator exists at ../antigravity-booster (local sibling repo, also on GitHub): the `agb` scheduler (lib/scheduler.mjs ~580 lines, zero-dep, depends on @adlc/core). Its proven mechanics are the design baseline:
- Ticket lifecycle: pending → building (worker in worktree) → gating (build+test) → prosecuting (cross-model refute) → [fixing → gating → prosecuting] → merging (sequential, rebase-first) → merged | failed.
- Event-driven readiness: a ticket dispatches the moment its edge predecessors MERGE (no wave barriers).
- Concurrency via pool semaphores (per-model quota pools in booster; v1 here needs only a single configurable concurrency cap, but the spec must define the pool abstraction so pools can return).
- Deterministic gates in the worktree and again post-merge on main (failed post-merge gate = revert).
- Two-strike regeneration informed by `adlc flail-detector` (a diagnosed flail skips the second strike; a clean one-off failure retries once with dead-ends appended).
- Blocked prosecutions fan out candidate fixes via `adlc consensus-fix` before a single-shot fix round.
- Control flow is code, judgment is models (ADLC D0): the scheduler is deterministic Node; no model decides sequencing.
Also read ADLC.md appendix D2 (fan-out mechanics: predict conflicts, don't resolve them; foundation paths pinned as rails) and the parallel-development conventions in docs/ (worktrees under .worktrees/, sequential merges, no parallel builds).

=== DECISIONS ALREADY MADE (do not relitigate) ===
1. Architecture: a NEW package, packages/fleet (@adlc/fleet), in this repo, following CONVENTIONS.md exactly (zero runtime dependencies, Node 18+ built-ins and @adlc/core via relative import only, bin/fleet.mjs thin CLI, lib/*.mjs pure logic, node:test offline tests, README with exit codes). antigravity-booster later becomes a consumer/sibling of this package; do not modify it in this ticket.
2. Deliverable: the specification AND an MVP implementation, in that order, with the spec gated before any implementation code is written.
3. Worker harness v1: Claude Code headless ONLY (`claude -p`/`--print`, non-interactive, permission mode suitable for unattended worktree builds). The scheduler must talk to workers through a WorkerAdapter seam (dispatch(prompt, {cwd, timeout, env}) → {output, exitCode} plus a charter/AGENTS.md provisioning hook) so codex exec / agy --print / opencode run adapters can be added later WITHOUT touching the scheduler. The adapter interface is a required section of the spec.

=== PHASE 1: SPECIFICATION (gate before code) ===
Write docs/specs/fleet-orchestration.md covering at minimum: goals/non-goals; the evaluation (what booster proved, what is agy-specific, what generalizes); plan source and schema; the WorkerAdapter interface; scheduler state machine and persistence/resumability across interruptions; worktree lifecycle (creation under .worktrees/<ticket-id>, branch naming, seeding, cleanup) per the repo's worktree conventions; gate integration (which adlc gates run where: merge-forecast pre-dispatch, rails-guard + ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT=1 inside worker worktrees, build/test gate per ticket, prosecution via the existing prosecute/adversarial-review path, runner evidence expectations); merge policy (sequential, rebase-first, post-merge gate, revert on failure); failure policy (two-strike, flail-detector, consensus-fix); concurrency model (single cap in v1, pool abstraction specified); observability (status file/CLI); threat model (a fleet of unattended writers is a new attack/blast-radius surface — cover rail enforcement in workers, trust-root freeze, and what a compromised/flailing worker can and cannot touch); and out-of-scope items (other harness adapters, quota-pool multiplexing, cross-repo fleets).
HARD REQUIREMENTS the spec must encode:
- Plan source is .adlc/tickets.json itself — the existing contract — NOT a new parallel plan format. The scheduler is a new backlog consumer, so it MUST exclude tickets with completed:true from its active set (repo invariant #104) and MUST respect scope/rails/edges/duration exactly as defined by @adlc/core.
- Tickets whose scopes overlap (core scopesOverlap) are serialized, never dispatched concurrently (merge conflicts are scheduled, not resolved).
- Single writer per partition: at most one worker may hold a given scope at a time; the main checkout is never written by workers.
- Deterministic control flow: no LLM call decides ordering, retries, or merges.
Gate the spec: `adlc spec-lint docs/specs/fleet-orchestration.md` exits 0, run `adlc premortem` against it and fold findings in, then STOP for explicit user approval (P1 G1) before writing any implementation code. Record the approval in the spec header.

=== PHASE 2: MVP IMPLEMENTATION (packages/fleet) ===
Implement per the approved spec:
1. lib/plan.mjs — load .adlc/tickets.json via @adlc/core, filter completed:true, compute ready set from edges + merged state, enforce scope-overlap serialization.
2. lib/scheduler.mjs — the event-driven loop with a configurable concurrency cap (default small, e.g. 2–3), state machine per the spec, resumable status persisted under .adlc/ (e.g. .adlc/fleet-status.json, in the evidence-ignore set).
3. lib/adapters/claude-code.mjs — the sole v1 WorkerAdapter: spawns `claude -p` with a builder charter (ticket body + scope + rails + dead-ends from prior strikes), cwd = the ticket's worktree, ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT=1 and ADLC_TICKET=<id> in env, timeout enforced.
4. lib/worktrees.mjs — create/remove/merge worktrees per repo conventions (may adapt booster's worktrees.mjs logic; keep zero-dep).
5. lib/gates.mjs — run the configured build/test command in the worktree and post-merge; wire flail-detector between strikes.
6. bin/fleet.mjs — `fleet run [--concurrency N] [--dry-run] [--tickets T..,T..]`, `fleet status`; exit codes per CONVENTIONS (0 ok / 1 operational / 2 gate-blocked).
Prosecution wiring may be a stub seam in the MVP if a full cross-model loop is out of reach — but the seam must exist and the spec must say what fills it.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each independently verifiable) ===
- AC1 (spec gated): docs/specs/fleet-orchestration.md exists with all required sections above; `adlc spec-lint docs/specs/fleet-orchestration.md` exits 0; premortem findings are reflected; the file records explicit user approval BEFORE any packages/fleet code was committed. VERIFY: run spec-lint; git log shows the spec commit precedes packages/fleet commits.
- AC2 (conventions): packages/fleet matches CONVENTIONS.md — package.json has zero runtime dependencies (no 'dependencies' beyond nothing; @adlc/core imported by relative path), type module, engines node >=18, bin wired. VERIFY: inspect package.json; grep imports.
- AC3 (scheduler correctness, offline): `npm test` in packages/fleet is green offline with a stubbed WorkerAdapter and stubbed git/gates, covering at minimum: (a) a ticket dispatches only after ALL its edge predecessors merge; (b) completed:true tickets are never dispatched; (c) the concurrency cap is never exceeded; (d) scope-overlapping tickets never run concurrently; (e) two-strike: first failure retries with dead-end context, second failure marks the ticket failed; (f) a diagnosed flail (stubbed flail-detector verdict) skips the second strike; (g) failed post-merge gate triggers revert; (h) status persists and a killed run resumes without re-dispatching merged tickets. VERIFY: run `npm test`; assert each case exists and exercises the real scheduler, not a mock of it.
- AC4 (adapter, offline): the claude-code adapter is tested via an injected exec stub — asserts the spawned argv contains -p/--print and non-interactive flags per the spec, cwd is the worktree, env carries ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT=1 and ADLC_TICKET, and timeouts/exit codes map to strike outcomes. No live claude invocation in tests. VERIFY: read the test; run it.
- AC5 (live smoke, manual-ok): a documented end-to-end smoke (README section) runs `fleet run --dry-run` against this repo's real .adlc/tickets.json and prints the computed ready set + dispatch plan without spawning workers or writing worktrees. VERIFY: run it; exit 0; output lists only incomplete tickets with satisfied edges.
- AC6 (no regression): the repo's full test suite still passes and no file outside this ticket's scope changed. VERIFY: `npm test` at root (or the repo's CI command) green; `git diff --name-only main...HEAD` ⊆ scope.
- AC7 (ADR): docs/adr/0010-adlc-fleet-orchestration.md pins the decisions above (new package, tickets.json as plan source, Claude Code-only v1, WorkerAdapter interface, deterministic control flow) with a Threat Model section. VERIFY: file exists; grep for 'WorkerAdapter' and '## Threat Model'.

Suppressions are denied. Out of scope (author follow-on tickets instead of building here): codex/agy/opencode/pi/cursor adapters, per-model quota pools, cross-model prosecution orchestration beyond the seam, GUI/status dashboards, changes to antigravity-booster.
title: Specify and build @adlc/fleet: parallel ticket orchestration on the ADLC (Claude Code workers v1)
